newsitem.title: ZAIRE: U.N. special envoy holds talks with Zaire's Kabila.
newsitem.headline: U.N. special envoy holds talks with Zaire's Kabila.

text.p: Laurent Kabila and his Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL) on Sunday pledged to fully cooperate with U.N. and other humanitarian agencies dealing with the refugee crisis in eastern Zaire, United Nations special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun said.

Sahnoun, accompanied by a special representative of the OAU (Organisation of African Unity), Mamadou Kamme, met Kabila as a delegation of Alliance leaders prepared to leave for Kinshasa to reassure the capital city's population about security.
He left Kinshasa after the talks for the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa to brief the OAU and then to New York where he would brief the Security Council on the situation in Zaire.
"I have a pledge from Kabila that the Alliance will cooperate with the U.N. on humanitarian issues," Sahnoun said.
"I did not go into details of every item. The main thing for me was to get his pledge of cooperation. In principle, I got this pledge," Sahnoun told reporters at Lubumbashi airport.
Sahnoun said he discussed the future of Zaire and the future of the Great Lakes region, the democratic process in Zaire and about the problem of (Rwandan) refugees in eastern Zaire.
"Kabila said he would be very cooperative and that he would take steps to help resolve the refugee issues," Sahnoun said.

"Measures will be taken to help the humanitarian agencies to fulfill their work and they will take their responsibility as a government to deal with this issue in a most humane way and try to help those refugees who might be having problems returning."
He said he and Kabila had also discussed the problems expected in setting up a broad-based government and the need for reconciliation in Africa's third largest country.

Asked whether Kabila was going to consult with the opposition leadership in Kinshasa, Sahnoun said: "He is having contact and he will continue with the contact. He has talked already with a number of opposition leaders. He did not close the door to any of these contacts."
Bizimah Karaha, the "foreign minister" of the AFDL, said South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki was due to arrive in Lubumbashi at 4 p.m. (1500 GMT).
